_comment: Manifest of pins that live DOWNSTREAM of this repo. Companion to versions.json:
versions.json records what each component last released; this file records where
each downstream repo pins the runtime (and third-party SDKs) in its own sources.
Consumed by .github/workflows/runtime-pin-bump.yml (opens repin PRs on a runtime
release, ABI-gated) and .github/workflows/pin-rot-canary.yml (checks SDK pins
still resolve AND still unpack a usable SDK). Spec + rationale:
docs/specs/runtime/downstream-pin-bump.md
To onboard a new vendor plug-in repo: add an entry under runtime_tag_pins with
every location its pin appears in, grouped by track. Nothing else to write --
the bump job is centralized here, not copied into each repo.

runtime_tag_pins.<repo>.tracks.<track>.auto_bump: true = repin automatically on a qualifying runtime release; false = human-owned, never touched
runtime_tag_pins.<repo>.tracks.<track>.locations: EVERY file the track's tag appears in. Written in ONE commit -- see atomicity note below.

_atomicity: A track is an ATOMIC GROUP. Each downstream repo runs a 'Rule-5' CI step that
hard-fails when its two pin locations disagree, so a bump MUST write every
location of the track in one commit. Updating one alone breaks that repo's CI.
_derived_values_are_not_pins: from DXR_RUNTIME_GIT_TAG. It is a CONSUMER of the pin, not a pin: CMake recomputes
it. Never list or edit derived values -- and note this derivation is exactly why
the bump is ABI-gated, since raising the pin raises that installer's minimum
_key_suffixes_are_safe: Tracks deliberately use SUFFIXED keys (DXR_RUNTIME_GIT_TAG vs _ANDROID vs _LINUX;
RUNTIME_REF vs _ANDROID). Bumping one can never rewrite another, because both
rewriters in scripts/downstream_pin_bump.py require a delimiter an underscore
cannot satisfy: cmake_set matches set(KEY followed by whitespace then a quote,
and yaml_env matches KEY followed immediately by a colon. Verified before the
android track was added (#1247) -- preserve this property if those regexes change.
_shape_constraint: The downstream Rule-5 checks regex the literal set(DXR_RUNTIME_GIT_TAG "vX.Y.Z"
shape. Rewrites must preserve it exactly -- no computed values, no indirection.

displayxr-leia-plugin.role: Leia SR display-processor plug-in (first vendor integration)

android.reason: The runtime's Android APK BUNDLES this plug-in (ADR-038), so the two ship as one artifact and must stay ABI- and build-config-matched. Unlike the windows track, no installer derives a MIN_RUNTIME_VERSION floor from this pin, so repinning costs nothing; the ABI gate still skips releases that change no plug-in ABI.

linux.reason: Deliberately held behind the Windows pin -- the Linux plug-in build tracks an older runtime on purpose. Human-owned; the bump job must never touch it.

displayxr-vendor-template.role: Scaffold every new vendor plug-in repo is generated from -- stale pins here seed into all future vendor repos, so it matters more than its commit count suggests

_comment_cnsdk: CNSDK is the Android counterpart of the SR SDK: a BUILD-TIME dependency of the
Leia plug-in, and a PACKAGING dependency of the runtime's leia APK variant (it
supplies the Java glue AAR + libleiaCore-loader.so + libleiaSDK-jni.so). The real
core, libleiaCore-impl.so, is dlopen'd from the on-device package and is never
redistributed -- so this pin governs the shim, not the engine.
Recorded here because nothing else tracks it: versions.json's membership rule is
'installable released asset', which CNSDK is not (it is not ours). Without this
entry the CNSDK version baked into a released APK is untraceable.
It is pinned in TWO workflows that must agree -- the plug-in builds against it and
the runtime packages it -- so a bump has to write both.
NOT CANARIED YET: pin-rot-canary.yml selects kind==lunarg_vulkan, so these rows
are recorded but unchecked. Adding a check is a follow-on and needs care -- the
release lives on the PRIVATE repo LeiaInc/CNSDK, so resolving it requires
LEIALOFT_GITHUB_TOKEN, and a 404 without that token is an auth failure, not a
rotted pin. Reporting the latter as the former is exactly the false-green this

excluded.displayxr-runtime: No LunarG step -- Vulkan comes from vcpkg (vulkan-headers + vulkan-loader + glslang[tools]) at a pinned commit. Immutable pins cannot rot; this is the pattern the others should migrate to (runtime#1029).
excluded.displayxr-runtime/.gitlab-ci/windows/mon: Inert Monado-era leftover carrying a stale LunarG URL. Not on any active CI path -- excluded so the canary does not report a failure nothing can act on.

_comment: The THIRD axis, and the one the other two miss.
versions.json     -- what each component last RELEASED.
runtime_tag_pins  -- where a repo pins the runtime to BUILD against.
consumer_floors   -- the OLDEST runtime a shipped consumer still WORKS on.
A vendor plug-in derives its floor from its build pin, so the first two
axes already cover it. A consumer that talks to the runtime purely over
the OpenXR wire -- the browser, the engine plug-ins, the CEF host -- has
no build pin at all: its real coupling is the extension SPEC_VERSIONs it
was compiled against. Nothing reconciled those against the runtime until
this block existed, and the cost was concrete. displayxr-browser shipped
a hand-typed MIN_RUNTIME_VERSION of 2.2.3 while actually requiring
XR_DXR_weave spec 8, which first shipped in runtime v2.8.0 -- so users on
v2.2.3..v2.7.x were told the prerequisite was satisfied and got a browser
whose weave path could not work. That is the exact failure the NSIS check
was added (browser#68) to prevent.
Consumed by scripts/drift_audit.py::check_consumer_floors, weekly via
.github/workflows/drift-audit.yml. Spec: docs/specs/runtime/downstream-pin-bump.md.
DESIGN RULE -- record WHERE TO LOOK, never the version numbers. They are
read live from each consumer's own headers on every audit, so this file
cannot drift from them. `requires` is spelled out ONLY for a consumer with
no readable header file (the browser -- see its entry).

_schema.gate: How the consumer behaves against a too-old runtime. hard = refuses or chains an upgrade. soft = degrades with a warning. none = no check at all.
_schema.spec_sources: Files to scan for `#define XR_DXR_<ext>_SPEC_VERSION <n>`. The ext segment is matched case-insensitively -- Unity writes XR_DXR_DISPLAY_INFO_SPEC_VERSION, the runtime writes XR_DXR_display_info_SPEC_VERSION -- and normalised to the runtime's lowercase header naming.
_schema.declared_floor: Where the consumer writes its minimum-runtime literal, if it has one. The audit compares it against the floor DERIVED from spec_sources.
_schema.requires: Escape hatch: an explicit {ext: version} map for a consumer whose headers are not readable files. Prefer spec_sources.
_monotonicity: Deriving 'which release first shipped spec N' binary-searches the runtime's
release tags, which assumes a SPEC_VERSION never decreases from one release
to the next. That has held for every XR_DXR_* extension and is the intended
contract; if one is ever walked back, the search reports the wrong floor.

displayxr-browser-pvt.role: Chromium fork; drives the display-processor weave over XR_DXR_weave. Windows + Android.
repo_note: PRIVATE repo, and the key is the repo the audit READS -- so it must name
-pvt, not the public displayxr-browser. The 2026-09 split put everything
that BUILDS (patches/, scripts/, installer/, workflows) in the private repo
and left everything that SHIPS (releases, assets, user-facing issues) on the
public one, which keeps its name. Both paths below moved with the source.
Reading a private repo needs the publish-bot App installation token that
drift-audit.yml already mints for displayxr-shell-pvt -- no new token. If
that mint ever degrades to the default GITHUB_TOKEN, this consumer goes
unreadable and the audit reports it rather than passing silently.
requires_note: Spelled out because this consumer vendors no header FILE -- it is a patch
series against Chromium, so XR_DXR_weave.h exists only after the patches
git grep -h '^+#define XR_DXR_weave_SPEC_VERSION' main -- patches | sort -u | tail -1
The audit cross-checks this number against requires_anchor's prose and
emits a note (not a finding) when it cannot confirm it there.

displayxr-unity.role: IUnityXRDisplay provider; loads the runtime directly and consumes XR_DXR_view_rig render-ready views.
displayxr-unity.gate_note: Detection is name-based, not version-gated: against a runtime missing XR_DXR_view_rig the plug-in emits a one-shot WARN and passes raw views through (no stereo). A floor violation degrades rather than fails -- worth reporting, not worth blocking.

displayxr-unreal.role: First-class UE HMD plug-in; direct runtime load + zero-copy atlas handoff.

displayxr-cef-host.role: Smallest worked example of driving the weave from an external present-owner. A reference to read, not a shipping product.

_excluded.displayxr-leia-plugin: Has a BUILD pin (DXR_RUNTIME_GIT_TAG) that its installer regex-derives MIN_RUNTIME_VERSION from, so runtime_tag_pins above already covers it. Listing it here would double-report.
_excluded.displayxr-demo-*: Built against a pinned runtime in their own CI and shipped as whole installers; no independent wire-protocol floor.
